QF.id: Taxation of Debt and Equity Products_11

question.text: Per the current NISM XII workbook (pages 135–136), which of the following STT (Securities Transaction Tax) rates is correctly matched with its transaction type?

answer.text: Sale of equity shares (delivery-based): 0.025% paid by the seller
Sale of equity shares (non-delivery/intraday): 0.001% paid by the seller
Sale of an option in securities where the option is exercised: 0.125% on intrinsic value, paid by the purchaser
Sale/redemption of equity mutual fund units: 0.025% paid by the seller

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the current NISM XII workbook (pp.135–136): delivery-based sale of equity shares is 0.100% paid by seller; non-delivery sale of equity shares is 0.025% paid by seller; sale/redemption of equity mutual fund units is 0.001% paid by seller; sale of an option in securities where the option is exercised is 0.125% on intrinsic value, paid by the purchaser. Only option C reflects a current source-backed match. The Trap: Option A understates delivery-based equity STT (current rate is 0.100%, not 0.025%). Option B understates non-delivery STT (current 0.025%, not 0.001%). Option D inflates equity MF redemption STT by a factor of ~25. Cross-Exam Context: NISM XII, VIII, and X-B all test current STT rates; further changes to STT on futures and options take effect from April 1, 2026.
